statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds. (1) For every vector c in r, len(c) = k, every entry c[i] with 0 <= i < len(c) satisfies 1 <= c[i] <= 9, the entries of c are pairwise distinct, and sum_{i=0}^{len(c)-1} c[i] = n. (2) For every k-element subset S of {1,2,...,9} with sum_{x in S} x = n, there is exactly one vector c in r whose set of entries {c[i] : 0 <= i < len(c)} equals S. (3) Conversely, for every vector c in r, its set of entries is a k-element subset of {1,2,...,9} with sum n. Equivalently, the collection of sets of entries of the vectors in r is exactly the set of all k-element subsets S of {1,2,...,9} satisfying sum_{x in S} x = n, with each such subset represented by exactly one vector.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60. All sums mentioned are mathematical sums of the listed entries.

statement: For every k and n satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, or panic.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every vector c in r, len(c) = k.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every vector c in r and every index i with 0 <= i < len(c), the entry c[i] satisfies 1 <= c[i] <= 9.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every vector c in r, the entries of c are pairwise distinct: for all indices i and j with 0 <= i < len(c), 0 <= j < len(c), and i != j, c[i] != c[j].
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every vector c in r, sum_{i=0}^{len(c)-1} c[i] = n.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, no two distinct positions of r contain vectors with the same set of entries: for all indices p and q with 0 <= p < len(r), 0 <= q < len(r), and p != q, the set {r[p][i] : 0 <= i < len(r[p])} is not equal to the set {r[q][i] : 0 <= i < len(r[q])}.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every k-element subset S of {1,2,...,9} whose element sum is n, there exists a vector c in r such that the set of entries of c is exactly S.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) <= C(9,k), where C(9,k) is the number of k-element subsets of {1,2,...,9}. Equivalently, len(r) <= 9!/(k!*(9-k)!).
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if n < k*(k+1)/2, then len(r) = 0. Here k*(k+1)/2 is the minimum possible sum of k distinct positive integers.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if n > k*(19-k)/2, then len(r) = 0. Here k*(19-k)/2 is the maximum possible sum of k distinct numbers chosen from {1,...,9}.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every vector c in r, if S is the set of entries of c, then the complement of S in {1,2,...,9} has size 9-k and its elements sum to 45-n.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(r) > 0, then k*(k+1)/2 <= n <= k*(19-k)/2.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if k*(k+1)/2 <= n <= k*(19-k)/2, then len(r) > 0.
preconditions: k and n are integers with 2 <= k <= 9 and 1 <= n <= 60.
